strategy.summary: On the buggy commit, scipy.stats.pearsonr with length-2 input where one array is constant takes the n==2 early-return path (sign-based r, pvalue=1) and never reaches the constant-input NaN handling, so it returns statistic=0.0, pvalue=1.0 while emitting ConstantInputWarning. The fix removes that n==2 special-case block so constant-input NaN handling applies; the added test test_length_two_constant_input expects ConstantInputWarning and r, p both NaN.

build_commands: Install SciPy per https://scipy.org/install/ (no exact command stated in evidence); a compiled SciPy build from the buggy commit 30a92651acb8 is required because the fix lives in scipy/stats/_stats_py.py and the test runs against the in-tree package
python dev.py build (or pip install -e . from the repo root at commit 30a92651acb8)
pinned_because: NumPy: documented only as 'SciPy is built to work with NumPy arrays'; no version constraint stated, so unpinned and chosen by the strategy
array_api_strict: installed only because the test suite's array-API backend parametrization (xp fixture) uses it; no version constraint in evidence
JAX: installed only because the test skip decorators reference jax.numpy; no version constraint in evidence; the bug itself is numpy-path behaviour and does not depend on JAX

strategy.reproducing_test: test_length_two_constant_input in scipy/stats/tests/test_stats.py (class TestPearsonr): x=[0.667, 0.667], y=[0.123, 0.456]; expects pytest.warns(stats.ConstantInputWarning, match 'An input array is constant') and xp_assert_close of r and p to NaN
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy commit 30a92651acb8, test_length_two_constant_input FAILS: stats.pearsonr returns statistic=0.0 and pvalue=1.0 instead of NaN, so the NaN assertion fails (ConstantInputWarning is emitted, so the warns block passes but the value assertion does not). On the fixed revision (the PR's merged state with the n==2 early-return block removed), the test PASSES: the warning is raised and r and p are both NaN.
strategy.numerical_probe: stats.pearsonr(np.array([0.667, 0.667]), np.array([0.123, 0.456])) and check whether statistic and pvalue are NaN
risks: The fix changes behaviour for n==2 non-constant inputs too: the removed block returned exact +/-1 for r; after removal these go through the general path, which may return values like 0.9999 rather than exactly 1.0 or -1.0. The existing tests test_length_two_pos1 and test_length_two_neg1 assert exact equality and may behave differently on fixed code; the PR's discussion indicates the author accepted 0.9999 vs 1.0 but the docs say only +/-1 are possible for n==2.
The JAX backend cannot run the item-assignment path; the added and modified tests are skipped for jax.numpy, so the transition can only be observed on the numpy (and array_api_strict) backends.

The failure is a wrong value (0.0/1.0 vs NaN), not a precision issue, so it should reproduce on any platform and does not need a specific architecture, sanitizer, or threading configuration as far as the evidence shows.
Dtype and precision of test inputs are not specified beyond xp.asarray defaults; the test uses default float64 for the list inputs under numpy.
Build-time details (compiler, BLAS backend, Python version) are not stated in the evidence and are left to the default SciPy build.
The exact pytest selector -k may match other tests in test_stats.py; if it does, narrow by class name (TestPearsonr) if needed.
The PR date is missing, so the exact buggy commit must be checked out by hash 30a92651acb8 rather than by date.

oracle.reference_source: docs of scipy.stats.pearsonr stating np.nan is returned for constant inputs
oracle.why: The test asserts NaN via xp_assert_close, which treats NaN equality as satisfied; the value being checked is the presence of NaN rather than a numerical tolerance.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision the n==2 early-return branch returns statistic 0.0 and pvalue 1.0 for [0.667,0.667] vs [0.123,0.456]; the ConstantInputWarning is still emitted so the pytest.warns block passes, but xp_assert_close(r, nan) sees 0.0 and fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the n==2 early-return removed, constant-input handling applies, the warning is emitted, and r and p are NaN, so both assertions pass.
